text:
Bonjour,
     After, doing a bit of an effort since last three days - i have drawn following conclusions.

       - We have two ways to unify all of the interaction of the COGLAB Team (both internally and externally).

              1 - Enhance/modify the existing website of the COGLAB by converting it into a portal (having podiums/forums for the discussion and brainstorming), which will be used by both COGLAB Team members for the internal chit-chat and also by the audience to comment/share their feedback over the on-going projects/activities of COGLAB by signing up to the forum.
              (What will it require) - An architectural re-design of the website and a ton of coding to enhance its operationability. Also, it can take upto several months for its completion.

              2 - Using a Social Media Manager (a third-party application) - and after doing an extensive search on the web, I have found some of the effective tools which are as follows.

<https://hootsuite.com> - HootSuite
<https://bufferapp.com/> - Buffer
<http://www.alternion.com/> - Alternion

              One of the above application will be used to handle all the social media platforms (FB, Twitter, G+, LinkedIN, etc) integrated in all-together. In this scenario, Slack and trello will be used for the internal communication and an 'Social Media Manager' App will be used to highlight, showcase and shine-up the on-going activites of COGLAB.
P.S. - Also the website will be handled separatly in the meantime as well.
              (What will it require) - An active and autonomous handler of the 'Social Media Manager' App and that's it. This scenario won't demand any coding/extra working and can be started from now-on. Alongside, it has alot to offer in terms of expanding and glorifying the appearance of the COGLAB in the social world.

     Now, i let it on to you guys to decide which option suits us the best. As far as my opinion is concerned, i am up for any of them.

text:
Salut Salman,

Thanks a lot for your research ! :simple_smile:

I bring some detail to complete your analysis :

- CogLab website is based on WordPress CMS.
They are many cool extension, like user registration
We can imagine, for example, a plugin based on this user base, to login on other tools (forum, wiki, ...)

- Internally, we have already a Slack and Trello account.

- Externaly, we must have a 
1) Wiki for documentation --> <http://coglab.fr/wiki/> (based on open source mediawiki, but requiere an other registration). Mediawiki have many plugin too. Maybe a way to connect with WordPress
2) Github for code --> <https://github.com/SCogLab> (it's ok, developper people have generally a GitHub account)
3) Forum for project discussion --> <http://vanillaforums.org/> (Vanilla seems available for our PHP serveur, and it's an open source project). But, for now, I'm not again test it, and we must found a trick to connect with WordPress / MediaWiki

- Social Media : I manage and connect all this tools (Facebook, Twitter, Google+, ...) on my way :wink:

attachments.title: Community Forum Software
attachments.text: Vanilla is forum software that powers discussions on 797,431 sites. Built for flexibility and integration, Vanilla is the best, most powerful community solution in the world.
